paper.citation: Hayden Helm, Ben Johnson, Carey E. Priebe, Query-efficient model evaluation using cached responses, arXiv:2605.07096.
paper.source_version: Retained ICML/non-anonymous transcription and source TeX.

purpose: Compare the printed Quench definitions, assumptions, and Theorem 2 with the Lean theorem surface, including explicit repairs of the retained source.

relation_definitions.exact: The source clause and Lean clause have the same mathematical content, modulo notation/encoding.
relation_definitions.equivalent_encoding: The mathematical content is equivalent, but Lean packages it in a structurally different form.
relation_definitions.lean_weaker_hypothesis: Lean assumes less than the source at this clause, so the Lean theorem is stronger here.
relation_definitions.lean_stronger_hypothesis: Lean assumes more than the source at this clause; this is a source-fidelity gap unless separately justified.
relation_definitions.lean_stronger_conclusion: Lean proves at least the source conclusion and additionally proves a stronger conclusion.
relation_definitions.lean_weaker_conclusion: Lean proves less than the source conclusion; this is a source-fidelity gap.
relation_definitions.different_quantifier_encoding: Lean makes an informal/asymptotic quantifier pattern explicit using an equivalent or stronger schedule/event formulation.
relation_definitions.derived_by_composition: No single source-shaped declaration exists, but the source clause follows from a checked composition of cited Lean declarations.
relation_definitions.source_repair: The retained source wording is inconsistent, false, or mismatched with its proof; Lean formalizes the repaired mathematical statement.
relation_definitions.proof_role_replaced: The printed proof-side lemma is not exposed literally; a different formal proof route removes or subsumes its role.
relation_definitions.missing: No Lean theorem surface was found for this source clause.
relation_definitions.supplementary: This Lean result goes beyond the printed source and is recorded for context, not source coverage.

rows.title: Inherited DKPS embedding concentration
rows.source_claim: For r=omega(n^3) and bounded response covariance, the maximum aligned perspective error is bounded by a cubic polynomial in (n^3/r)^(1/2-delta) with high probability.

clauses.source_clause: Inherited Theorem 1 states max_i ||psiHat_i-psi_i|| <= Poly3((n^3/r)^(1/2-delta)) with high probability.
clauses.lean_clause: Quench consumes Acharyya2025 Frobenius configuration concentration and then uses norm_config_le_ConfigFrobError to obtain every row bound.
clauses.note: This avoids treating the inconsistent Acharyya v1 2,infinity display as literally proved while still supplying the rowwise control Quench uses.

clauses.source_clause: Technical spectral assumptions are inherited from Acharyya.
clauses.lean_clause: The current inherited chain has fixed rank/floor/cap assumptions but no hsmall, hpolar, or redundant finite-stage rate-zero premise.
clauses.note: The DK/YWS improvements made the inherited theorem closer to the paper assumption surface.

clauses.source_clause: Theorem 1 bounds max_i ||psi-hat_i - psi_i|| over the n reference models.
clauses.lean_clause: The rate theorem is proved for a fixed model collection; the Quench capstones instead re-derive the bound stage by stage for a growing sample with the target augmented into the matrix, using the same ConfigPerturbation machinery.
clauses.note: The paper's proof needs the bound for the target model too, which is not one of the n reference models it applied Theorem 1 to.

rows.review: Quench uses the current Acharyya Frobenius concentration theorem plus the rowwise norm bound, which supplies exactly the max-row control needed by the Quench proof without claiming the disputed Acharyya v1 display literally.
rows.notes: The rate endpoint is proved but not consumed downstream: Quench needs the growing-sample, target-augmented regime. See gap theorem1-rate-not-instantiated.
rows.next_action: Either generalize the rate theorem to a growing sample with an augmented target, or keep the divergence recorded; the capstones do not depend on the choice.

rows.title: DKPS perspectives are a raw-stress minimizer
rows.source_claim: The d-dimensional DKPS representations are a solution to argmin over z of the sum of (||z_i - z_j|| - D_{ii'})^2.

clauses.source_clause: The perspectives are a minimizer of the raw stress sum over (||z_i - z_j|| - D_{ii'})^2.
clauses.lean_clause: Acharyya2024.rawStress defines that objective and Acharyya2024.MDS its minimizer set, but no Quench module references either.
clauses.note: The Eq. (1) estimator is formalized; it is simply not the one Quench uses.

clauses.source_clause: Theorem 1 bounds max_i ||psi-hat_i - psi_i|| for these perspectives.
clauses.lean_clause: The imported Acharyya 2025 bound and the whole Quench chain use the classical-MDS perspectives of the response distance matrix.
clauses.note: The source does not establish that a raw-stress minimizer satisfies the classical-MDS bound, so the two readings are not interchangeable.

rows.review: Equation (1) defines DKPS by raw stress while every result the paper proves about psi-hat comes from a classical-MDS concentration theorem. The formalization follows the classical-MDS reading because that is what Theorem 2's proof consumes, and the divergence is recorded rather than assumed away.
rows.next_action: None; recorded as a source-fidelity divergence.

rows.title: Q-, m-, and all-budget query efficiency
rows.source_claim: Eventually the DKPS predictor risk is no larger than the subset-score baseline; m-query efficiency quantifies over all subsets of size m and full query efficiency quantifies over all m<M.

clauses.source_clause: Q-query efficiency: exists N such that for all n>N the DKPS predictor risk is <= the baseline risk.
clauses.lean_clause: QQueryEfficient has exactly exists N, forall n>N, Risk(h n)<=Risk(h' n).

clauses.source_clause: m-query efficiency quantifies this over every subset Q of cardinality m.
clauses.lean_clause: mQueryEfficient quantifies over all Finset Q with card=m and gives a subset-specific threshold.

clauses.source_clause: Full query efficiency quantifies over every m<M.
clauses.lean_clause: The higher-level predicates preserve this quantifier order; high-probability analogues add confidence events without changing the source deterministic definition.

rows.review: The deterministic source predicates and their high-probability analogues are explicit. The all-subset lift preserves the source quantifier order.

rows.title: Tie-averaged nearest-neighbor score estimator
rows.source_claim: Average the full-benchmark scores of every reference model tied at the minimum estimated perspective distance.

clauses.source_clause: The displayed estimator averages scores over every reference model tied at the minimum estimated perspective distance.
clauses.lean_clause: tieAverageNN / yNNTieAverage_paper implement the literal tie average.

clauses.source_clause: The proof text subsequently chooses one f* in argmin and treats its full score as yHat_NN.
clauses.lean_clause: yNN_paper separately implements the single-selected-neighbor proof object.
clauses.note: Keeping both definitions makes the source display/proof mismatch explicit; the preferred source-facing estimator is the tie average.

rows.review: The preferred formal estimator is the literal displayed tie average. A separate yNN_paper follows the proof text and chooses one minimizer, making the source mismatch explicit rather than conflating them.

rows.title: Benchmark score is Lipschitz in population perspective distance
rows.source_claim: There exists gamma>0 such that score differences are at most gamma times perspective distance.

clauses.source_clause: There exists gamma>0 such that full-score differences are bounded by gamma times perspective distance for the chosen query subset.
clauses.lean_clause: Theorem2 takes exactly the fixed-Qsub inequality; LipschitzScore packages the all-subset variant.

clauses.source_clause: gamma is positive.
clauses.lean_clause: Some public certificates normalize a witness using max(gamma,1), eliminating a separate positivity burden without weakening the inequality.

rows.review: Lean stores the displayed Lipschitz inequality and can replace any valid constant by max(gamma,1), so public certificates do not require a redundant positivity proof for the supplied witness.

rows.title: Positive probability of every target-centered neighborhood
rows.source_claim: The prose claims positive mass for every compact subset and calls this equivalent to positive mass for each target-centered ball.

clauses.source_clause: The prose first says Pf has nonzero measure on all compact subsets of model space.
clauses.lean_clause: Lean does not formalize this literal clause.
clauses.note: The literal statement is false because the empty compact set has measure zero, and positive mass for arbitrary compact sets is much stronger than needed.

clauses.source_clause: The paper then calls this equivalent to: every target-centered ball has positive probability.
clauses.lean_clause: PerspectiveFullSupport formalizes the positive-mass-in-every-perspective-ball property used by the proof.
clauses.note: This is the mathematically relevant support condition.

clauses.source_clause: Denseness should yield a nearby reference model with high probability as n grows.
clauses.lean_clause: Compact perspective range + iid reference sampling + PerspectiveFullSupport prove uniform high-probability coverage.

rows.review: Lean formalizes the ball-support property actually consumed by the proof. Compactness plus iid reference sampling then proves uniform high-probability nearest-reference coverage.
rows.notes: The false all-compact-subsets wording is not propagated into the theorem API.

rows.title: Nearest-neighbor MSE can be made arbitrarily small with high probability
rows.source_claim: For every epsilon>0 there are sufficiently large sampling/model budgets for which MSE(yhat_NN)<=epsilon with high probability.

clauses.source_clause: For every epsilon>0 there exists a budget triple (n,m,r) with MSE(yHat_NN)<=epsilon with high probability.
clauses.lean_clause: highProb_mse_nn_le fixes Qsub and abstracts m,r into the stage-indexed estimator/rate; for every epsilon and confidence delta it produces an n with probability >=1-delta.

clauses.source_clause: Assumption 1 supplies score smoothness.
clauses.lean_clause: The theorem takes the fixed-Qsub Lipschitz inequality and gamma>0.

clauses.source_clause: Assumption 2 supplies nearby reference models.
clauses.lean_clause: The theorem takes high-probability uniform coverage; compact-iid-fullSupport wrappers derive it from the repaired support assumption.

clauses.source_clause: Theorem 1 supplies representation error c(n,m,r,d)->0.
clauses.lean_clause: infiniteFixedSubsetMSE and finiteFixedSubsetMSE derive the concentration from iid raw responses through the CMDS/Davis--Kahan perturbation chain; only the conditional intermediates take it as a premise.
clauses.note: The derivation is at a replicate schedule stronger than the source r = omega(n^3).

clauses.source_clause: The paper proof moves from a pointwise target error bound to MSE.
clauses.lean_clause: Lean explicitly requires measurable concentration/coverage events and proves a uniform-in-target bound before integrating.
clauses.note: These are formal analytic obligations omitted from the prose proof, not extra statistical content.

clauses.source_clause: The theorem is stated for the DKPS perspectives of Eq. (1).
clauses.lean_clause: The estimator uses the classical-MDS perspectives, matching the Theorem 1 bound the proof consumes rather than the raw-stress definition.
clauses.note: Recorded as gap dkps-definition-raw-stress-vs-cmds; see Q26-EQ1.

rows.review: The printed conclusion is proved end to end by infiniteFixedSubsetMSE and finiteFixedSubsetMSE for the literal tie-averaged estimator built from raw cached responses, with the representation concentration derived rather than assumed. The verdict remains GAP because the derivation needs a population nondegeneracy floor and a replicate schedule above the source rate, and because the perspectives are classical MDS rather than the Eq. (1) raw-stress minimizer.
rows.next_action: Weaken the replicate schedule toward the source r = omega(n^3) and replace the absolute eigenvalue floor by a residual-gap condition.

rows.title: Eventual high-probability improvement over subset-score baseline
rows.source_claim: When m<M and the subset-score baseline has positive MSE, nearest-neighbor DKPS prediction is query-efficient with high probability.

clauses.source_clause: If m<M and MSE(yHat_Q)>0, yHat_NN is query-efficient relative to yHat_Q with high probability.
clauses.lean_clause: Lean requires the positive baseline MSE and proves the eventual high-probability risk comparison.

clauses.source_clause: The prose proof leaves measurability and the uniform-target step implicit when passing from pointwise NN error to MSE/risk.
clauses.lean_clause: The source-facing Lean theorem requires measurable high-probability concentration/coverage events (or a measurable subevent certificate) before integration.
clauses.note: These are explicit analytic premises not stated in the paper theorem.

clauses.source_clause: The source also assumes m<M.
clauses.lean_clause: The strongest fixed-subset Lean theorem drops m<M because the proof never uses it; all-subset wrappers reintroduce the source budget quantification where appropriate.

clauses.source_clause: The source theorem is initially existential in one budget triple.
clauses.lean_clause: Lean also proves eventual fixed-subset, m-query, and all-budget high-probability predicates with the source quantifier order.

clauses.source_clause: Query efficiency is claimed for all m < M, not only for one fixed subset.
clauses.lean_clause: infiniteAllQueries and finiteAllQueries conclude HighProbQueryEfficient, which quantifies over every budget below the benchmark cardinality and every subset of that size.

rows.review: The printed conclusion is proved at the paper's full quantifier level by infiniteAllQueries and finiteAllQueries for the raw-response estimator, with the representation concentration derived rather than assumed. The verdict remains GAP for the same hypothesis excess recorded on Q26-T2A.
rows.notes: The formal proof supplies the missing uniform-target/measurability step before integrating pointwise squared error to MSE.
rows.next_action: Weaken the replicate schedule toward the source r = omega(n^3) and replace the absolute eigenvalue floor by a residual-gap condition.

rows.title: End-to-end finite raw-response query efficiency
rows.source_claim: Theorem 2 at the finite model-class scope: the paper's proof derives the representation error from Theorem 1, so discharging it is inside the printed argument rather than beyond it.

clauses.source_clause: No printed theorem starts from the complete finite raw cached-response sampling model.
clauses.lean_clause: FiniteSubsetData/Assumptions and finiteFixedSubset/finiteAllQueries discharge concentration, realization, and query-efficiency end to end.

rows.review: The finite realization of Theorem 2. This row previously read as an extension beyond the paper theorem surface, which inverted the layering: the paper's proof of Theorem 2 derives its representation error from Theorem 1, so discharging that premise is inside the printed argument. What genuinely exceeds the source is the explicit sampling and regularity interface and the replicate schedule.
rows.next_action: Weaken the replicate schedule toward the source r = omega(n^3) and replace the absolute eigenvalue floor by a residual-gap condition.

rows.title: End-to-end compact-infinite query efficiency
rows.source_claim: Theorem 2 at the compact-infinite model-class scope: the paper's proof derives the representation error from Theorem 1, so discharging it is inside the printed argument rather than beyond it.

clauses.source_clause: The printed theorem does not specify a uniform infinite-population concentration mechanism.
clauses.lean_clause: InfiniteSubsetData/Assumptions and infiniteFixedSubset/infiniteAllQueries add compact/cover regularity and prove the corresponding end-to-end theorem.

rows.review: The compact-infinite realization of Theorem 2. This row previously read as an extension beyond the paper theorem surface, which inverted the layering: the paper's proof of Theorem 2 derives its representation error from Theorem 1, so discharging that premise is inside the printed argument. What genuinely exceeds the source is the explicit sampling and regularity interface and the replicate schedule.

rows.title: Theory-practice OLS bridge
rows.source_claim: The experiments use OLS/ensemble regressors although Theorem 2 proves nearest-neighbor query efficiency.

clauses.source_clause: The paper experiments use OLS but the printed theorem is nearest-neighbor based.
clauses.lean_clause: The OLS theorem family is an additional theory/practice bridge under explicit affine-risk assumptions.

rows.review: The OLS formalization is an additional theorem family with explicit affine-risk assumptions; it is not evidence for the printed nearest-neighbor Theorem 2 and is not required for source coverage.
rows.notes: Tracked because it explains the paper theory/practice boundary.
